subject: Prefix thundering causing retry surge / BrightBridge production timeouts
messages:
From: BrightBridge SRE <sre@brightbridge.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Liu <sara@brightbridge.com>, Tim O'Neal <tim.oneal@brightbridge.com>
Date: 2027-05-21T09:12:34-07:00
Subject: Production timeouts — tokens returning 504 / 429 surge

Hi Rishi,

We're seeing a sustained spike in 5xx/429s across our inference endpoints starting ~08:45 PDT. Latency suddenly jumps from ~120ms p50 to multi-second tails, and a downstream retry loop is amplifying traffic — currently ~3x normal qps. We attached a small bundle of logs and a CSV with prefix distribution slices.

Quick facts:
- Affected route: /v1/generate (model: redwood-3b-v1)
- Error pattern: internal 504s from the inference tier + upstream 429s returned to our services
- First seen: 2027-05-21T08:42:12-07:00
- Current impact: degradations across our web tier, some users getting blocked

Can you triage? If this is a cache/batching regression you shipped yesterday, we need mitigation and an ETA. We're preparing a P1 incident bridge and may escalate to execs shortly.

Attachments: prod-logs-20270521.tar.gz, prefix-summary-20270521.csv

- Sara (BrightBridge SRE)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: BrightBridge SRE <sre@brightbridge.com>
Cc: Sara Liu <sara@brightbridge.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-21T09:18:05-07:00
Subject: Re: Production timeouts — tokens returning 504 / 429 surge

Thanks for the heads up, Sara — sorry you're hitting this. I'm escalating to our on-call infra and engineering leads now. Monica, can you pick this up and confirm whether the recent prefix-KV batching change could explain a thundering prefix or cache eviction pattern?

Immediate asks:
- Confirm if there's a known rollout/flag change in the last 24h
- If it's a KV-cache thrash, do we have a fast rollback or a per-customer routing bypass?
- We should stand-up a short bridge: redwood.ai/incident/BRG-3421 (I'll DM the bridge link)

I'll update BrightBridge as we know more.

— Rishi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, BrightBridge SRE <sre@brightbridge.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-21T09:44:12-07:00
Subject: Re: Production timeouts — tokens returning 504 / 429 surge

On Fri, May 21, 2027 at 09:18, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Monica, can you pick this up and confirm whether the recent prefix-KV batching change could explain a thundering prefix or cache eviction pattern?

Quick triage summary (on-call):
- We observed unusual eviction storms for very short prefixes (<= 6 tokens) starting at 08:40 PDT; eviction rate correlates with the spike window.
- Root cause hypothesis: an index bug in the batching coalescer with a bad fallback path that drops prefix caching, causing many concurrent requests to miss the KV cache and regenerate heavy KV writes. That in turn floods the local batch queues and causes timeouts -> 504s -> client retries.
- Evidence: attached partial stack traces and per-shard eviction counters.

Immediate mitigations taken (09:30 PDT):
1) Locked the new batching coalescer flag to off for all prod clusters (rolled back a passive rollout).
2) Temporarily throttled per-customer burst to limit amplification for BrightBridge specifically.
3) Added a short-lived route to fall back to a warmed variant with prefix-agnostic cache (routing rule: customer_id == BRG -> model_variant = redwood-3b-v1-warm).

Impact: error rate dropped ~40% in the first 12 minutes post-mitigation, tail latencies improving but still elevated for long-running requests. We're continuing to drain queues and monitor.

Attachments referenced: mitigation-runbook-v1.md (internal runbook), partial logs included.

Next steps: full postmortem & fix for coalescer index. I will post updates to the bridge.

— Monica
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Tim O'Neal <tim.oneal@brightbridge.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Sara Liu <sara@brightbridge.com>
Cc: BrightBridge SRE <sre@brightbridge.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-21T10:05:50-07:00
Subject: Re: Production timeouts — tokens returning 504 / 429 surge

Appreciate the quick action. Two asks from BrightBridge leadership: 1) can we get a temporary credits/SLR for customer impact window (08:40–09:30 PDT)? 2) We need a clear ETA for the permanent fix — we can't have repeated prefix eviction regressions.

Also: our app logged multiple user-facing errors and some queued background jobs were retried 5x, compounding our load. We need firm remediation steps besides the rollback.

- Tim (BrightBridge Head of Platform)
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Tim O'Neal <tim.oneal@brightbridge.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-21T11:02:10-07:00
Subject: Re: Production timeouts — tokens returning 504 / 429 surge

Thanks Tim — understood. Rishi, I'll coordinate the credits and formal SLR paperwork with Finance; Markus, can you provide conservative ETA for a fix and a mitigation playbook we can share with BrightBridge execs? I want to avoid vague timelines.

Markus, suggested mitigation doc from infra: short-term (today): routing bypass + throttles (already applied), medium-term (48–72h): patch to coalescer index + more aggressive prefix warmers, long-term: algorithmic limits on concurrent KV fill for small prefixes. Are those realistic?

— Laura
VP, Product Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-21T12:30:44-07:00
Subject: Re: Production timeouts — tokens returning 504 / 429 surge

Short answer: yes. Technical plan and conservative ETA: 
- Hotfix (rollback + safer fallback): already rolled back at 09:30 PDT; immediate mitigation is in prod and reduced error rate ~40% within 15 minutes.
- Patch (48 hours): a code fix to the coalescer's index bounds checking + unit tests covering short-prefix behaviour. Target: 2027-05-23T18:00:00-07:00 for canary, 2027-05-24 for full rollout after validation.
- Longer-term (2–4 weeks): rate-limiter per-prefix fill and prefix-warming heuristics to prevent cold storms.

I'll prepare a short slide for the BrightBridge execs and the SLR request. Also attaching a short mitigation-runbook-v1.md for ops to follow.

— Markus
Staff Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Tim O'Neal <tim.oneal@brightbridge.com>, Sara Liu <sara@brightbridge.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-23T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Prefix thundering causing retry surge / BrightBridge production timeouts

Tim/Sara — following up with a concise update:
- Short-term rollback and routing bypass reduced the error surface and stabilized traffic within ~30 minutes of mitigation.
- We've scheduled the patch (coalescer index fix) for canary on 2027-05-23 18:00 PDT and full rollout pending validation.
- Laura is coordinating credits/SLR; expect an email from Finance by EOD.
- We're drafting a post-incident timeline and will share a write-up once the patch is validated.

Thanks for patience — we'll keep the bridge open for the canary and circulate the postmortem with concrete next steps.

— Rishi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
